setup.zh: 立冬这天晌午，马三来收租。院子里摊着那头鹿，当门摆着一挂下水，娘坐在门槛里头等着。马三眯起眼睛：「黑松岭的鹿，姓什么？」
setup.en: Noon on the Start of Winter: Ma San comes for the rent. The deer lies spread over the yard, the offal right by the door, and your mother sits waiting inside the threshold. Ma San narrows his eyes: "The deer of Black Pine Ridge — what's their name?"

recap.zh: 皮抵了去年的欠，肉抵了今年的租，角也叫马三拿走了，他连爷爷的弓都摘了下来；娘问了一句「下水呢」，你编了一个吃饼、问「弓呢」的鬼，马三把弓扔了回来。娘摸了摸你的"围脖"，什么都没问。
recap.en: The hide went for last year's arrears, the meat for this year's rent, Ma San took the antlers too — and took grandfather's bow down off the wall. Your mother asked, "And the offal?"; you made up a ghost that eats flatbread and asks "Where's the bow?", and Ma San threw the bow back. Your mother touched your "scarf" and asked nothing.

zh: 皮，抵去年的欠；肉，抵今年的租。
en: The hide for last year's arrears; the meat for this year's rent.
"The bow that shot a Ma deer — its name is Ma too."

story.zh:
马三是晌午来的。

马小宝跟在后头，啃着一只酱鸭腿。

马三站在沈家院子里，看着那一地摊开的鹿，眼睛眯了起来。

他拎起那张鹿皮抖了几抖，问道：「黑松岭？」

小满他爹老老实实地道：「黑松岭。」

马三把鹿皮往肩上一搭，道：「皮，抵去年欠下的；肉二十斤，抵今年的。」

又拿短棍把那一地的肉拨了一遍，眼睛一眯：「一头鹿，四条腿。怎么只有三条？」

马小宝在他爹身后嚷道：「爹，阿禾说了，是头瘸腿的小母鹿！」门口有人「噗」地笑出了声。马三看看那对比门框还宽的角，又看看儿子，一挥手：「母鹿长角？……称肉！」少的那一条腿，他懒得追；二十斤肉，总是够的。

家丁上来称肉，称满了二十斤，秤杆翘得跟马三的下巴一样高。

秤称完了，马三却没有走。他背着手，绕着那一地摊开的东西转了一圈，转到那对鹿角跟前，站住了，拿短棍敲了敲，

道：「这对角，不错。」

小满他爹道：「三爷喜欢，您拿去。」

马三道：「不是我喜欢。」他转过身来，看着他，慢悠悠地道：「黑松岭，是谁家的山？」

小满他爹一怔。

马三道：「蒙山是马家的。黑松岭在不在蒙山上？」

他爹道：「……在。」

马三道：「那黑松岭的鹿，姓什么？」

院子里静了。半个村子的人都看着小满他爹。他的嘴唇动了两动，一个字也没说出来。他那双昨儿拉弓都不抖的手，这时候又抖了起来。

马三道：「山上的树姓马，山上的兔子姓马，山上的风都姓马。黑松岭上跑出来的鹿，倒姓了你家的姓？」他拿短棍往地上那堆肉一划，划了一个圈，「肉，我拿回去；角，我拿回去；皮，抵租。这叫公道。」说着眯起眼睛，往屋里瞧了一眼，瞧的是墙上那张缠着牛筋的旧弓，「还有一样。马家的鹿，是拿这张弓射的。射马家鹿的弓——也姓马。」

他一低头，侧着身子跨进门槛，伸手便把那张弓从墙上摘了下来。

小满他爹扑通一声跪倒：「三爷！租交了！您说的，一张皮——」马三道：「皮是皮，弓是弓。」他掂了掂那张弓，「这叫连本带利。」他也并不真打算拿走——弓挂到马家墙上，不过一截木头，明年的皮子倒没了着落。他要的是沈老大跪着，再多添几样，往后年年记着怕。

小满站在他爹身后，两只拳头不知什么时候已经攥紧了。他比马三矮了两个头，马三手里还有那根包铁皮的短棍——打不过，就跑，娘说的。可这一回，他跑了，弓便没了。一张鹿皮，二十斤肉，崖上吊着的那根布绳，溪边那一箭，肩上那团凉下去的毛——统统抵了租，统统白搭，弓还是要姓马。他看了他娘一眼。他娘站了起来。

她没有走到马三跟前去，就站在门槛里头，说道：「三爷。下水呢？」

马三一愣，手里拎着弓，低头瞧了瞧当门那一挂鹿下水，皱起了眉头：「下水？」她道：「下水，也是马家的鹿身上的。三爷连弓都拿了，下水也拿去罢。」

马三瞧着那挂下水，又瞧了瞧她，脸上的横肉跳了两跳。这一挂下水，他要拿，往后石坳村的人提起马三，便要说一句「连人家的下水都拎走了」；他不拿，方才那番「马家的鹿」的话，便说得不大圆。他想了一会儿，大手一挥，道：「下水，赏你们了！」

她道：「谢三爷。」说完便坐下了，坐回门槛里头，两只手拢在袖子里。

马三拎着那张弓，低头看那弓背，看那一道一道缠着的牛筋，不知怎的，看出了神。然后他走回小满他爹跟前，压低了声音道：「黑松岭……你们进去了，还出来了？」他顿了一顿，「里头，还有什么？」
story.en:
Ma San came at noon.

Ma Xiaobao followed behind, gnawing a braised duck leg.

Ma San stood in the Shens' yard looking at the deer spread over the ground, eyes narrowing.

He picked up the hide, gave it a few shakes, and asked: "Black Pine Ridge?"

Xiaoman's father said honestly: "Black Pine Ridge."

Ma San slung the hide over his shoulder. "The hide covers what you owed last year; the twenty jin of meat covers this year."

Then he prodded through the meat on the ground with his club, and his eyes narrowed. "One deer, four legs. Why are there only three?"

Ma Xiaobao piped up behind his father: "Dad, Ahe said — it's a little doe with a lame leg!" Someone at the gate snorted with laughter. Ma San looked at the antlers, wider than the doorframe, then at his son, and waved a hand: "A doe with antlers? …Weigh the meat!" The missing leg he couldn't be bothered to chase; twenty jin of meat there was, either way.

The servants came up and weighed out twenty jin of meat, the steelyard beam tilted as high as Ma San's chin.

When the weighing was done, Ma San still didn't leave. Hands behind his back he circled the things laid out on the ground, stopped at the antlers, and tapped them with his club.

"Fine antlers, these," he said.

Xiaoman's father said, "If Third Master likes them, take them."

Ma San said, "It's not that I like them." He turned and looked at him, and said, slow and easy: "Black Pine Ridge — whose mountain is it?"

Xiaoman's father froze.

Ma San said, "Mount Meng is the Mas'. Is Black Pine Ridge on Mount Meng?"

His father said, "…It is."

Ma San said, "Then what's the name of the deer from Black Pine Ridge?"

The yard went quiet. Half the village was looking at Xiaoman's father. His lips moved twice; not a word came out. Those hands that hadn't trembled drawing a bow the day before trembled again now.

Ma San said, "The trees on the mountain are named Ma, the hares are named Ma, even the wind is named Ma. And a deer run out of Black Pine Ridge takes your family's name?" He drew a circle round the pile of meat with his club. "The meat, I take; the antlers, I take; the hide goes for the rent. That's fair." Then he narrowed his eyes and looked into the house — at the old sinew-wrapped bow on the wall. "And one more thing. The Ma deer was shot with that bow. A bow that shoots a Ma deer — is named Ma too."

He ducked his head, turned sideways through the doorway, and reached up and took the bow down from the wall.

Xiaoman's father dropped to his knees with a thump. "Third Master! The rent's paid! You said, one hide —" Ma San said, "A hide's a hide, a bow's a bow." He weighed the bow in his hand. "This is called principal plus interest." Nor did he really mean to carry it off — on a wall at the Ma house the bow was just a stick of wood, and next year's hides would have nowhere to come from. What he wanted was Shen the elder on his knees, adding a little more, and remembering to be afraid every year after.

Xiaoman stood behind his father, both fists clenched without his knowing when. He was two heads shorter than Ma San, and Ma San still had that iron-sheathed club — if you can't win, run: his mother had said so. But this time, if he ran, the bow was gone. A deer hide, twenty jin of meat, the cloth rope hanging down the cliff, that arrow by the stream, the curl of fur on his shoulder gone cold — all of it paid in rent, all of it for nothing: the bow would still be named Ma. He glanced at his mother. His mother stood up.

She didn't go to Ma San; she stood right there inside the threshold and said: "Third Master. And the offal?"

Ma San started, the bow in his hand, and looked down at the string of offal in front of the door, frowning. "The offal?" She said, "The offal's off a Ma deer too. Third Master has taken even the bow — take the offal as well."

Ma San looked at the offal, then at her, and the fat on his face jumped twice. Take the offal, and ever after Shi'ao folk speaking of Ma San would add, "he even carried off their offal"; leave it, and his speech about "the Ma deer" didn't quite hold together. He thought a while, then waved a large hand. "The offal — I make you a gift of it!"

She said: "Thank you, Third Master." And sat down again inside the threshold, hands tucked in her sleeves.

Ma San, holding the bow, looked down at its back, at each wound strip of sinew, and somehow looked a long time. Then he walked back to Xiaoman's father and lowered his voice: "Black Pine Ridge… you went in, and came out again?" He paused. "What else is in there?"

label.zh: 踩爹的脚后跟，抢着装傻
label.en: Tread on Father's heel and play the fool

exits.means: plays dumb, says there is nothing in there, scared, hides what they saw

story.zh:
他爹张嘴就要说。他爹这个人，这辈子不会撒谎，人家问什么，他便答什么。他要是把那道摔不死人的山谷、谷里会发亮的草和会响的银叶子说出来，马三明天便会带着二十条猎狗、几十个家丁进去，把那道山谷翻个底朝天。

小满站在他爹身后，轻轻踩了一下他爹的脚后跟。

他爹一愣，嘴张着，没出声。小满抢着开了口——一面说，一面缩着脖子，两只手抱着胳膊，浑身上下抖得像一片秋风里的树叶——「三爷！里头……里头黑乎乎的，下大雨，我掉沟里了，差点就死了！还有鬼！」

马三眉头一皱：「鬼？」

「有个白衣服的！」小满抖得更厉害了，「没有脚，飘着走，头发老长老长，一直拖到地上——三爷，那地方真不能去，我爷爷就是在那儿没的！」

院子里好几个婆娘已经拿手捂住了嘴。

马三道：「……白衣服的？」

「还吃饼！」

马三一怔：「鬼吃饼？」

「吃得可香了！」小满拿手比了一比，「我娘烙的饼，这么厚一张，它三口就吃完了，一面吃还一面嫌难吃！」

说到这里，他的眼睛往马三手里一瞟，声音忽然压低了，压得只剩一口气：「……吃完了饼，它还问我——」

马三道：「问你什么？」

小满道：「它问：『弓呢？』」

马三没有动。过了半晌，他的嗓子有点发干，道：「……你看清它的脸了？」

小满道：「没脸。就一把白胡子。」

马三的手，这才抖了一抖。小满便接着抖，从头顶抖到脚跟，抖到后来，牙齿也咯咯地打起架来：「它说，那张弓，是它的。谁拿了它的弓，它就跟谁回家。」他心里却一面抖，一面暗道：银月，对不住。你要是醒着，准要咬我。抖着抖着，他自己也分不清了：这一身抖，有几分是装的。

马三的脸，先是红，跟着变紫，又跟着变黑，最后变成了那一种颜色。他瞧着手里那张弓，像瞧着一条盘起来的蛇。半晌，他把弓往小满他爹怀里一扔，扔得又急又慌，倒像那弓烫手，骂了一声：「晦气！」

马小宝却不怕。他跟在他爹身后，走过小满身边，忽然伸出那只油乎乎的手，一把揪住了小满脖子上的「围脖」，凑到鼻子底下闻了闻：「一股狗味儿。不过毛倒是软——拿回去，给我娘缝个领子。」小满两只手死死捂住了它，脸上却抖得更凶了：「小宝哥，这皮子……是黑松岭里捡的，就在那白胡子脚底下。」马小宝的手像给火燎了一下，缩了回去，在衣裳上蹭了三遍，道：「……谁稀罕。一张狐狸皮，我家要多少有多少。」

马三已走到了门口，又回过头来，冲着满院子的人道：「都听着。打今儿起，谁靠近断碑一步，腿打断。」说罢一跺脚，走了。

马小宝跟在后头，走过老周家门口，瞧见阿禾蹲在篱笆里头，一脚踢翻了她搁在墙根的那只腌白菜坛子：「小母鹿？」坛子在地上滚了两滚，那一个秋天的白菜叶子，撒了一地。

马家的人走远了，看热闹的人也散了。他爹把那张弓挂回墙上，挂了两回才挂稳，又蹲下去，把那挂下水捧了起来，捧得很小心。他道：「……这个，给老周家。赔白菜。」

他娘道：「嗯。」

他爹又道：「棉袄……」

他娘道：「不急。」

说着把两只手往袖子里拢了拢。她那件棉袄，是嫁过来那年做的，袖子短了一截，一拢，手腕便露在外头，冻得发红。

她把小满叫到跟前，看了他很久，才道：「那个白衣服、没有脚、吃饼的鬼。」

小满只得招认：「……娘，那是我编的。」

「嗯。编得不好。」他娘顿了一顿，「鬼不吃饼。下回说它吃香火。」

小满一愣：「为什么？」

他娘道：「鬼吃饼，马三会想，那是个饿死鬼，饿死鬼好打发，扔两张饼就是了。鬼吃香火，那就是有人供着的，有人供着的鬼，马三惹不起。」

他娘伸出手来，替他把脖子上那条「围脖」理了一理。她是看不见银月的——可她的手，偏偏停在了银月的背上，停了一停。小满低头一看，只见围脖里那只昏迷的小狐狸，耳朵轻轻地动了一下。

他娘说道：「小满，这条围脖，挺暖和的吧。」

她什么都没问。他爹捧着那挂下水，站在门口，朝黑松岭那边望了一眼，道：「断碑不让靠近了。这个冬天……」他娘道：「这个冬天，还长着呢。」
story.en:
His father opened his mouth to tell him. His father couldn't lie to save his life; whatever you asked, he answered. Had he told of that valley a boy could fall into and live, its glowing grass and its ringing silver leaves, tomorrow Ma San would take twenty hounds and dozens of servants in and turn that valley upside down.

Standing behind his father, Xiaoman gently trod on his father's heel.

His father started, mouth open, no sound. Xiaoman got in first — talking while he hunched his neck, hugging his arms, shaking all over like a leaf in the autumn wind: "Third Master! In there… it's pitch dark, it was pouring, I fell in a ditch, nearly died! And there's a ghost!"

Ma San frowned. "A ghost?"

"There was one in white!" Xiaoman shook harder. "No feet, it floats along, hair long, long, trailing right down to the ground — Third Master, you really can't go there, my grandpa died in there!"

Several women in the yard clapped hands to their mouths.

Ma San said: "…One in white?"

"It eats flatbread too!"

Ma San blinked. "A ghost that eats flatbread?"

"Wolfed it down!" Xiaoman held his hands apart. "My mum's flatbread, this thick, gone in three bites, and it complained it was awful the whole time!"

At this his eyes flicked to Ma San's hand, and his voice suddenly dropped, till it was only a breath: "…When it finished the bread, it asked me —"

Ma San said, "Asked you what?"

Xiaoman said, "It asked: 'Where's the bow?'"

Ma San didn't move. After a long moment, his throat a little dry, he said: "…Did you see its face?"

Xiaoman said, "No face. Just a white beard."

Only then did Ma San's hand shake. So Xiaoman kept shaking, from the crown of his head to his heels, until even his teeth were chattering: "It said that bow is its bow. Whoever takes its bow, it goes home with them." But inside, shaking all the while, he thought: Yinyue, sorry. If you were awake you'd bite me for sure. Shaking and shaking, he could no longer tell how much of it was put on.

Ma San's face went red, then purple, then black, and at last turned that one particular colour. He looked at the bow in his hands as if at a coiled snake. After a long moment he flung it at Xiaoman's father, hasty and flustered, as though it burned, and swore: "Bad luck!"

Ma Xiaobao, though, wasn't afraid. Following behind his father, passing Xiaoman, he suddenly reached out a greasy hand, grabbed the "scarf" round Xiaoman's neck and held it to his nose. "Smells of dog. Soft fur though — I'll take it home and have a collar sewn for my mother." Xiaoman clamped both hands over it, while his face shook harder than ever: "Xiaobao-ge, this pelt… I picked it up in Black Pine Ridge, right at the feet of the white beard." Ma Xiaobao's hand jerked back as if singed. He wiped it on his clothes three times over, and said: "…Who wants it. One fox pelt — my family has all we like."

Ma San had reached the gate. He turned back and told the whole yard: "Listen, all of you. From today, anyone who goes one step near the broken stele gets his legs broken." With that he stamped and left.

Ma Xiaobao, following, passed the Zhous' gate, saw Ahe crouched inside the fence, and kicked over the jar of pickled cabbage she'd set by the wall: "A little doe?" The jar rolled twice on the ground, and a whole autumn's cabbage leaves spilled across the dirt.

The Mas had gone off into the distance, and the onlookers had drifted away. His father hung the bow back on the wall — it took two tries to hang it straight — then crouched and gathered up the offal, carefully. He said, "…This goes to the Zhous. To make good the cabbage."

His mother said, "Mm."

His father said, "The coat…"

His mother said, "No hurry."

And she drew her hands into her sleeves. That padded jacket of hers had been made the year she married in; its sleeves were a length too short, and when she drew her hands in, her wrists showed outside, red with cold.

She called Xiaoman over and looked at him a long while before she said: "That ghost in white, with no feet, that eats flatbread."

Xiaoman could only confess: "…Mum, I made that up."

"Mm. Badly." His mother paused. "Ghosts don't eat flatbread. Next time say it eats incense."

Xiaoman blinked. "Why?"

His mother said, "A ghost that eats flatbread — Ma San thinks, a starved ghost; starved ghosts are easy to get rid of, throw it two flatbreads. A ghost that eats incense — somebody's worshipping it, and a ghost somebody worships, Ma San can't afford to cross."

His mother reached out and straightened the "scarf" round his neck. She couldn't see Yinyue — yet her hand stopped right on Yinyue's back, and rested there a moment. Xiaoman looked down: the unconscious little fox inside the scarf had moved one ear, very slightly.

His mother said, "Xiaoman, that scarf — nice and warm, is it?"

She asked nothing. His father, holding the offal, stood at the gate and looked once toward Black Pine Ridge. "The stele's out of bounds now. This winter…" His mother said, "This winter is a long one yet."

exits.means: tells the truth about the ridge, lets father answer honestly

story.zh:
他爹张嘴就要说。他爹这个人，这辈子不会撒谎，人家问什么，他便答什么，这是他最大的本事，也是他最大的毛病。他要是把那道摔不死人的山谷、崖根底下那个孩子说出来，马三明天便会带着二十条猎狗、几十个家丁进去，把那道山谷也篦一遍，篦得比他娘梳头还细。

小满在后头伸脚去踩他爹的脚后跟——踩空了。他爹已经一五一十地说了：「里头的树，比外头高一倍。鹿，比前山的大一圈。就是路不好走，下起雨来——」

马三的眼睛一下子亮了，亮得像两盏刚点上的油灯。他掂了掂手里那张弓，忽然把它往小满他爹怀里一塞，道：「大一圈？好。弓，你留着。黑松岭的鹿，今年起，也姓马了——马家的狗不进那块碑，你进。明年开春，你拿这张弓，进去给马家打。」说罢转身便走。

小满看着他爹怀里那张弓。弓是留下了，可从今往后，它射出去的每一支箭，都姓马。

马小宝跟在他爹身后，走过小满身边的时候，冲他挤了挤眼睛：「哟，沈小满，还活着呢？命挺硬啊。」小满低下头道：「托小宝哥的福。」马小宝很满意。小满不太满意。

马家的人一走，他娘便把小满拉进屋，关上了门，看着他，看了很久，才叹了口气，道：「你爹那张嘴。娘管了二十年，没管住。」

她伸出手来，替他把脖子上那条「围脖」理了一理。小满登时愣住了。她是看不见银月的，在她眼里，那不过是一条灰不溜秋的旧狗皮——可她的手，偏偏停在了银月的背上，停了一停。小满低头一看，只见围脖里那只昏迷的小狐狸，耳朵轻轻地动了一下。

他娘说道：「小满，这条围脖，挺暖和的吧。」

她什么都没问，转身去灶间了。
story.en:
His father opened his mouth to tell him. His father couldn't lie to save his life; whatever you asked, he answered — his greatest skill and his greatest failing. Had he told of that valley a boy could fall into and live, and the child at the foot of its cliff, tomorrow Ma San would take twenty hounds and dozens of servants in and comb that valley too, comb it finer than his mother combed her hair.

Xiaoman reached out a foot behind to tread on his father's heel — and missed. His father was already telling it, every detail: "The trees in there are twice as tall as outside. The deer, a size bigger than the front hills'. Only the going's bad, and when it rains —"

Ma San's eyes lit up at once, like two lamps just lit. He weighed the bow in his hand, then shoved it into Xiaoman's father's arms. "A size bigger? Good. Keep the bow. From this year, the deer of Black Pine Ridge are named Ma too — the Ma dogs won't pass that stele, but you will. Come spring, you take this bow in there and hunt for the Mas." And he turned to go.

Xiaoman looked at the bow in his father's arms. The bow had stayed — but from now on, every arrow it loosed would be named Ma.

Ma Xiaobao, following his father, winked at Xiaoman as he passed. "Well, Shen Xiaoman, still alive? Tough little life you've got." Xiaoman lowered his head. "All thanks to you, Xiaobao-ge." Ma Xiaobao was very satisfied. Xiaoman was not.

The moment the Mas were gone his mother pulled Xiaoman inside and shut the door, and looked at him a long time before she sighed. "Your father's mouth. Twenty years I've tried to govern it, and never managed."

She reached out and straightened the "scarf" round his neck. Xiaoman froze. She couldn't see Yinyue; to her it was a scruffy old grey dog pelt — yet her hand stopped right on Yinyue's back, and rested there a moment. Xiaoman looked down: the unconscious little fox inside the scarf had moved one ear, very slightly.

His mother said, "Xiaoman, that scarf — nice and warm, is it?"

She asked nothing, and turned and went into the kitchen.
